transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. Can you start by telling me what's been bothering you or what brought you in to see me?

Well... I guess I'm just having trouble getting things done lately. I can't really keep my mind on a task long enough to finish it anymore. Even when it's important. 

I do computer support, and... I'll start tracing a client's network problem, and then maybe ten minutes later I'll realize I've just reread the same log entries three times. And I still won't know what they actually say. So... yeah. That's what brought me in.
Have you always had this kind of trouble focusing, even back in school as a kid, or is this a new change from how you used to be?

I guess it's... not really new. It's always been like this. 

My mother actually still jokes about it. She brings up my old grade school report cards sometimes. She says the teachers always wrote that I was bright, but... I never stayed in my seat. Or I'd just blurt out answers. And I was always losing my homework, even when I actually did it. 

So... yeah. It's not a new thing.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling persistently sad, down, or losing interest in things you'd normally enjoy?
No... I wouldn't say that. I'm not sad. Just... frustrated with work, mostly. But no, I haven't lost interest in things or anything like that.
Besides at work, do you notice this same trouble focusing or staying on task causing problems in other parts of your life, like at home or in relationships?

Yeah... it affects other things. 

I used to have a more structured job, but since I lost that... things have been rough. I've lost some freelance clients recently. And I missed out on a senior service-manager role I was up for. 

It's just... people don't really trust me to follow through on things right now. My reputation has taken a hit. It's caused some tension at home, too, with my wife. We've had to worry about money because of it. So... yeah. It's not just work.
Do you currently notice yourself feeling restless, fidgety, or having trouble sitting still, or acting or speaking impulsively before thinking things through?

I suppose so... yeah. Sitting still isn't really my strong suit. 

If I'm sitting with a client, or... even just at a chess meeting... my leg is usually bouncing. Or I'll be clicking a pen, twisting a cable tie around in my fingers. I don't really realize I'm doing it until... well, until somebody finally gives me that look.
Thinking back to before you were about 12 years old, can you tell me if you were already having these same kinds of struggles—like trouble focusing, fidgeting, or acting impulsively—at that age?

I suppose... yeah. My mother actually still brings it up sometimes. She jokes about my old grade school report cards. 

She says they always noted that I was bright, but... that I never stayed in my seat. Or I'd blurt out answers. And I was always losing my homework, even when I had actually done it. So... yeah. I guess it's been like this for a while.
